title: NRT annotations, #nullable, and compiler warnings
hook: Nullable reference types are a compiler conversation: you annotate intent, the compiler tracks not-null versus maybe-null, and it warns when the code disagrees. It does not rewrite IL to ban null.

sections.heading: Nullable context
sections.prose: SDK templates for modern .NET, including .NET 10, set <Nullable>enable</Nullable> in the project file. That turns on both the annotation context (string versus string?) and the warning context (CS8600-family diagnostics). Older libraries may still be nullable-oblivious: their string parameters are treated as neither annotated nor warned, which is why a Redis client or AWS SDK method can return string and still be null. File-level #nullable enable, disable, restore, and #nullable enable warnings let you migrate a large worker without boiling the ocean. Interviews want the project switch first, pragmas for islands, not a pile of !.

snippets.label: Annotate a cache lookup
snippets.explanation: BuildKey is non-nullable: a null tenantId is a warning. Redis miss is string?. Pattern matching updates null-state so json.Length is safe.

sections.heading: What the warnings actually mean
sections.prose: Null-state analysis labels each expression not-null or maybe-null as it walks the method. Warning on a non-nullable variable means you assigned something maybe-null (CS8600 / CS8601). Warning on a nullable variable means you dereferenced it while it was still maybe-null (CS8602). Both say the same thing: the code does not match the annotation. Fixes Microsoft documents are: add a check, fix the ? or !, add an analysis attribute, initialize the field, or verify the project setting. Silencing with #pragma warning disable CS8602 is not a strategy; it is how an auth header parser ships an NRE to production.

sections.heading: Initialization and records
sections.prose: Non-nullable reference fields must be assigned by every constructor path. Object initializers do not count unless the member is required (next topic). A common Redis options class with public string Connection = null!; is a smell: you told the compiler to stop looking. Prefer a constructor, a required property, or string? until the config binder has run. C# 14 field-backed properties still obey the same null-state rules on the backing storage — new syntax, same analysis.

interviewTakeaways: <Nullable>enable</Nullable> is the project-wide switch; #nullable is per file.
Warnings encode mismatched intent, not a runtime null ban.
if (x is not null) / is { } narrows null-state; the compiler is not psychic across helpers unless you annotate them.
commonPitfalls: Leaving a library nullable-oblivious and trusting its string return as non-null.
Initializing with null! on every field to ‘make the build green.’
Dereferencing SQS Message.Body without a check because the AWS types were annotated loosely.

jsTsCorrelations.note: strictNullChecks is the TS analogue of <Nullable>enable</Nullable>. Both are compiler modes, not runtime checks.
